question: Which alternatives could remove an apparent benefit from exact motor gradients, and which prior methods already cover the proposed implementation?

sources.title: Geometric design of electric motors using adjoint-based shape optimization
sources.authors: Luca Scotzniovsky, Ru Xiang, Zeyu Cheng, Gabriel Rodriguez, David Kamensky, Chris Mi, John T. Hwang
sources.evidence_read: Author-hosted paper: abstract, introduction and computational implementation section.
sources.finding: Free-form deformation, PDE mesh warping and electromagnetic FEM are combined with exact derivatives; CSDL automates adjoint derivative computation.
sources.implication: End-to-end differentiable motor shape optimization is already prior art. Our candidate contribution must rest on controlled cost comparisons and useful design freedom, not the existence of a differentiable implementation.

sources.title: Robust Shape Optimization of Electric Devices Based on Deterministic Optimization Methods and Finite Element Analysis With Affine Decomposition and Design Elements
sources.evidence_read: Primary arXiv abstract and publication metadata; detailed experiment conditions not audited.
sources.finding: Gradient-based FEM geometry optimization without remeshing, including a PM synchronous machine, is compared with stochastic methods such as particle swarm optimization.
sources.implication: A gradient-versus-stochastic motor comparison is not itself new. Review its detailed target, design dimension and accounting before claiming a benchmark gap.

sources.title: Optimal torque control of permanent magnet synchronous machines using magnetic equivalent circuits
sources.authors: Wolfgang Kemmetmueller, David Faustner, Andreas Kugi
sources.evidence_read: Author-hosted postprint, abstract and model description.
sources.finding: A nonlinear magnetic equivalent circuit represents saturation and nonsinusoidal behavior and supports constrained current optimization, with experimental control validation.
sources.scope_limit: This is current/control optimization, not freeform shape optimization or a matched FEM optimizer benchmark.
sources.implication: Saturation and torque harmonics alone do not prove simple physical models inadequate. Include a nonlinear, angle-aware reduced magnetic model where feasible, not only global scaling laws.

sources.title: Electrical machines surrogate-based design optimization based on novel waveform targeting strategy with improvement of the computational efficiency
sources.authors: Farnam Farshbaf Roomi, Abolfazl Vahedi, Amin Nobahari
sources.evidence_read: Publisher full text: abstract and training-cost section.
sources.finding: Waveform-targeted Kriging uses sampled motor waveforms rather than only aggregate output fits. Its cost comparison includes FEM training samples and model-training time.
sources.scope_limit: Prediction accuracy at a stated R-squared threshold is not equal-target optimization timing against an adjoint.
sources.implication: Use a waveform-aware surrogate as a credible baseline candidate; assess derivative/sign and candidate quality on held-out designs, and charge acquisition/training costs.

sources.title: A globally convergent method to accelerate large-scale optimization using on-the-fly model hyperreduction: application to shape optimization
sources.finding: Projection and hyperreduction are adapted along the optimization trajectory inside a trust-region framework, including snapshot/model construction in the cost.
sources.scope_limit: Demonstrations are fluid shape optimization, not electric motors.
sources.implication: An adaptively calibrated reduced model can be stronger than a fixed offline surrogate. Retain this as a baseline design principle; do not transfer its published speedup to motors.

sources.title: Spline-Based Rotor and Stator Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
sources.evidence_read: Primary paper and pinned public implementation b145aaf4ab1a6424828bc941eaf172f48fa0d458.
sources.finding: Provides the nonlinear motor reproduction anchor; combines adjoints, shape parameters and scaling laws.
sources.implication: Reproduce the recorded model before changing objectives or fixing envelope/current controls for the later causal comparison.

sources.title: Combined Parameter and Shape Optimization of Electric Machines with Isogeometric Analysis
sources.evidence_read: Primary comparison section and tables, inspected in the feasibility pass.
sources.finding: Parameter and shape comparisons motivate useful-shape-freedom testing. Its evolutionary comparison has different settings/hardware, and some shape-only comparisons relax torque constraints.
sources.implication: This supports a controlled comparison question, not a claim that no earlier fair benchmark exists.

baseline_plan: Exact-gradient constrained optimization and the same optimizer with finite differences, as a diagnostic of derivative computation cost.
A calibrated, angle-aware reduced physical model; include nonlinear material effects when its representation permits them.
A waveform-targeted surrogate with online refinement, counted from the first FEM training sample.
Competitive derivative-free trust-region search and CMA-ES under the same design space and budget.
Separate nested-design-space ablation: small engineering basis versus additional shape controls, keeping physical constraints and validation targets matched.
unresolved_before_novelty_claim: Full experiment audit of the 2018 deterministic-versus-stochastic motor paper and its follow-on work.
Whether a published equal-target, equal-hardware comparison already spans many shape dimensions and adaptive reduced-model baselines.
Which reduced physical/surrogate implementation can represent the selected ICEM shape family without unfairly restricting the competitor.
A final current-literature search before manuscript submission.
